data.section: Multibagger Case Studies & the "Second-Order Thinking" Process

title: multibagger_case_studies › Multibagger Case Studies & the "Second-Order Thinking" Process

body:
- **The same pattern, different outcomes:** Suzlon (2005–08) and Inox Wind/renewables, the infra/power capex boom of 2007–08 (Lanco, GVK, JP Associates **[UNVERIFIED specific outcomes]**), and Yes Bank / DHFL as "Bajaj Finance look-alikes" in lending **[UNVERIFIED]** all had a policy or sector tailwind, fast growth and a high multiple. What separated them from Eicher, Radico and Bajaj Finance was mostly **leverage, governance and the capital-allocation discipline of the promoter**. That fits Mayer's "avoid debt so drawdowns aren't permanent" rule.
- **Practical base rate:** with about 2–4% of stocks creating all net wealth, a "multibagger playbook" should be judged on portfolio outcomes (a few big winners paying for many losers) and on position-sizing rules that survive 50–90% drawdowns, not on hit rate.
- **Hindsight trap:** each case study selects on the outcome. For each signal (policy shift, competitor distress, capex announcement), the counterfactual cases where it fired and the stock failed should be logged too, for example the solar/wind PLI and the China+1 chemical names that derated in 2022–25.
